Round numbers half away from zero

Source: R/round.R
pub_round.Rd

Rounds as pubflow's tables do, and as SAS's ROUND() does: if the first digit after the last one kept is 5 or more, the number is rounded up in magnitude.

Usage

pub_round(x, digits = 0)

pub_format_num(x, format)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector.

digits

A whole number >= 0: the number of decimal places.

format

A number format as in tables: either a whole number of decimal places (at most 324) or a sprintf() format with exactly one %.nf, %.ne or %.ng conversion and any other text, e.g. "%.1f %%" or "Mean: %.2f". The number is rounded to n decimal places (f), n + 1 significant digits (e) or n significant digits, at least 1 (g). Flags and widths as in "%+.2f" or "%5.2f" are not supported.

Value

pub_round(): a double vector with the attributes of x (NA, NaN and infinite values stay as they are).

pub_format_num(): a character vector with the names and dimensions of x; NA and NaN give NA, infinite values "Inf" or "-Inf".

Details

Functions

  • pub_round() returns the rounded numbers, e.g. to compare a result with a threshold.

  • pub_format_num() returns the text that a table cell with this number format shows (see pub_cell_text()), e.g. for numbers in a text.

Why not round()?

round(), formatC() and sprintf() round the number as the computer stores it (in binary), and exact ties go to the even digit. As most decimals can't be stored exactly, this often looks wrong: 2.675 is stored as 2.67499999999999982, so they give 2.67.

pub_round() and pub_format_num() use the digits of the number's decimal text instead (the 15 significant digits that as.character() shows and a table cell stores), so ties round as expected. A result of zero has no sign.

xpub_round(x, 2)round(x, 2)
0.1250.130.12
2.6752.682.67
-2.675-2.68-2.67
9.995109.99
-0.00100

See also

pub_cell_text(), pub_table()

Examples

x <- c(0.125, 2.675, 1.005, 0.285, -2.675, -0.001, 9.995)
round(x, 2)
#> [1]  0.12  2.67  1.00  0.28 -2.67  0.00  9.99
pub_round(x, 2)
#> [1]  0.13  2.68  1.01  0.29 -2.68  0.00 10.00
pub_format_num(x, 2)
#> [1] "0.13"  "2.68"  "1.01"  "0.29"  "-2.68" "0.00"  "10.00"
formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)  # the binary value, ties to even
#> [1] "0.12"  "2.67"  "1.00"  "0.28"  "-2.67" "-0.00" "9.99" 

pub_format_num(c(0.5, 2.5, -0.5), 0)
#> [1] "1"  "3"  "-1"
pub_format_num(c(0.125, 999.5), "%.2g")
#> [1] "0.13"  "1e+03"
pub_format_num(12.25, "%.1f %%")
#> [1] "12.3 %"

# Numbers in text
pub_format_num(mean(c(98.25, 99.1)), "Mean assay: %.2f %%")
#> [1] "Mean assay: 98.68 %"
